title: This summer I'll go to the sea
title_target: През лятото ще отида на море
goal: Talk about the future with one small word — **ще** — and learn that its negative does not use *не* at all, but a separate form: **няма да**.
bekal: forming the future with **ще** + the present form
negating it with **няма да**, not *не ще*
naming the seasons and travel plans

dialogs.title: Диалог — Summer plans
dialogs.intro: Ivan and Ani talk about the holidays. Notice the little word **ще** that keeps coming back — and that the verb after it doesn't change at all from the present.

lines.speaker: Иван:
lines.id: What are you going to do this summer?

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: I'll go to the seaside. I've never seen the Black Sea.

notes: **The Bulgarian future is one of the simplest in Europe: put ще before the present form, done.** *Работя* (I work) → *ще работя* (I will work). The verb doesn't change at all. No special forms, no changing helper verbs, no exceptions.

⚠️ **The negative is NOT не ще.** That form exists in old and literary language, but everyday Bulgarian uses **няма да**: *Няма да работя* — I won't work. Note that *няма* here doesn't change with the person; the verb does. This is the most typical mistake in this unit.
**Ще itself never changes.** *Ще отида, ще отидеш, ще отиде, ще отидем…* One word for everyone. Compare English with its *will* and *shall*, or French, which demands six new endings.
**Ще е and ще бъде are both correct for "will be".** *Ще е* is lighter and heard more often in conversation; *ще бъде* is a bit more formal. For the negative: *няма да е* or *няма да бъде*.

**През means "during, in" for periods of time.** *През лятото* (in the summer), *през зимата* (in the winter), *през седмицата* (during the week), *през нощта* (at night). ⚠️ Note that seasons are always **definite** after *през*.
**Ако means "if", and the verb stays in the present** even when talking about the future: *Ако искаш, ще дойда* — if you want, I'll come. Not *ако ще искаш*. Exactly the same as in English.
**Ще видим — "we'll see" — is the universal way to put off a decision**, just like "we'll see" in English, with all its vagueness.

**Никога не съм виждала is the perfect tense**, covered fully in Unit 16. For now, notice just one thing: *виждала* ends in **-ла** because Ani is a woman. If Ivan said it, the form would be *виждал*.

grammars.title: Ще — one word for the whole future
body: The present form isn't touched at all. All you add is *ще* in front.
after: Small words like *се, ми, го* stand **between ще and the verb**: *ще **се** видим* (we'll see each other), *ще **ти** кажа* (I'll tell you).

Look at the third row: some verbs come in pairs — *отивам* (going, repeated) and *отида* (go once, completed). For the future, the second form is almost always used. This is the start of the aspect system, the main topic of level A2.

grammars.title: Няма да — the future negative
body: The negative is not built from *ще*, but from *няма*, which you already know as "there isn't".
after: **Няма да never changes**, whoever the subject is. The person is carried by the verb after *да*, just as with *трябва да* in Unit 8.
⚠️ Future questions put *ли* after the verb: *Ще дойдеш ли?* (Will you come?). For the negative: *Няма ли да дойдеш?* (Won't you come?).

sections.title: Seasons, weather and periods of time

blocks.text: ⚠️ **Пролет and есен are feminine words ending in a consonant** — two of the six exceptions mentioned in Unit 2. Their article is still **-та**, and the stress moves onto it: *пролетта* (*pro-let-TA*), *есента* (*eh-sen-TA*).

Bulgaria has four very distinct seasons. Winter in Sofia drops to minus ten degrees Celsius and snow stays for weeks; summer can reach thirty-five. If you come from a mild or tropical climate, **зимата** will be your biggest shock — far bigger than the grammar.

**Хайде** (*HAI-deh*) is the invitation word you'll hear most in Bulgaria — "come on, let's go". It is also used to wrap up a phone call: *Хайде, чао!* It was borrowed from Turkish and exists all over the Balkans, so you'll recognize it again in Greece, Serbia and Romania.

blocks.title: Черно море — the coast nobody expects
items: Bulgaria's Black Sea coast stretches for more than three hundred kilometers, and in summer the whole country moves there. **Варна** is a big port city with a museum holding the oldest gold jewelry in the world — six thousand years old, older than Egypt and Mesopotamia.
**Несебър**, a small town on a rocky peninsula, has more than forty medieval churches within a few hundred meters. **Созопол** is quieter, with wooden houses and narrow lanes.
A sentence that will instantly fire up any Bulgarian: *Кое е най-хубавото място на морето?* (What's the best place on the coast?) Everyone has an answer, and no two are the same.

exercises.prompt: Change into the future negative with няма да.
Put the words in the right order.
items: ще / през / отида / лятото / на море
We'll see each other on Friday.

answers: Ще работя днес. — Ти ще четеш книгата. — Тя ще отиде на море. — Ние ще бъдем в София. — Ще имам време. — Ще се видим утре.
Няма да работя утре. — Няма ли да дойдеш? — Няма да е скъпо. — Няма да имаме време. — Няма да се видим в петък.
През лятото ще отида на море. — Няма да реша днес. — Ще пътуваме с влак. — Колко дни ще останем? — Ще видим.
Какво ще правиш утре? — Ще отида на море. — Няма да е скъпо. — Ще се видим в петък. — Няма да мога.
